name: Crucible HeatHand Foundry Weld Gauntlet
description:
Heavy-duty split-cowhide shell with aluminized dorsal panels that reflect radiant heat up to 800°C. Stitched with Kevlar-analog thread in bright orange — visible against grime, easy to spot on a factory floor. The cuffs are long and flared, reinforced with a stiffened carbon-fiber band to resist wrist injuries from dropped stock. Chrome-arm wearers typically cut the left glove at the wrist seam and resecure it with the integrated snap-tab closure.

Worn through hard shifts, most units show blackened finger pads and scorch marks around the knuckle reinforcements within weeks. A glove that looks used is a glove that's working.
functionality: Rated for foundry and arc-weld environments; aluminized panels reflect radiant heat, Kevlar stitching resists cut and puncture, snap-tab cuff allows single-hand donning. Chrome-arm snap tab permits secure attachment over prosthetic wrist flange.
what_it_says: You work with fire and you're not pretending otherwise.
story_hooks: A worker's chrome forearm keeps overheating — the snap-tab cuff is trapping heat against the prosthetic housing, and someone swapped the standard lining for a non-breathable knockoff.
A pair of these gloves is found at a crime scene — the scorch pattern on the fingers matches a very specific industrial torch model no longer in production.
A Shelf fabricator is quietly modifying these gloves with smuggled sensor-fiber, turning them into crude haptic rigs.
